Dear Americans,

I am a soldier of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, and I want to tell you something.

Freedom is not measured in dollars. Freedom is not measured by the price of diesel in your car’s tank.

Freedom is measured by a nation’s willingness to fight for its country, its people, and its right to exist.

We Ukrainians know the price of freedom. We pay it in blood. Every single day.

We will continue striking Russian military targets. We will continue fighting Russian invaders on land, at sea, and in the sky. In Ukraine and wherever Russia wages its war against us.

Because we are not fighting for money, oil, or comfort.

We are fighting for our homeland. For our future. For our FREEDOM.

And we will never surrender it.

Nearly one in three Indian schools lacked internet access in the 2025–26 academic year.

The Education Ministry’s UDISE+ report recorded internet facilities in 67.4% of schools. It lists 14,66,682 schools nationwide, with internet available in 9,89,191. That leaves 4,77,491 schools without it.

Starlink could help connect remote schools and give teachers and students access to more learning resources. A child’s opportunities should not depend on whether a broadband cable reaches their classroom. 

Starlink has already connected more than 6 million students worldwide. This is another powerful reason to support Starlink in India.
